::: notes
Picks up from the checklist: "…as the saying goes, standards are like toothbrushes. Everybody wants one. Nobody wants to use anybody else's."

1:05.

Before the click there's only a toothbrush, held out: "want to use mine?" That's every standard's offer. Everyone sorts their bricks their own way, and nobody adopts someone else's system.

Click: the box appears, the toothbrush packs into its lid, and the title turns. "So datom keeps its own." Point at the box: it's datom's travel kit, its own toothbrush packed in the lid. The hashes, manifest, version log and parquet are the checklist you just saw; they stay in the kit, and datom applies them. You only ever call `datom_write()` and `datom_read()`.

Every build records its exact pieces and its instructions, without anyone filing anything. It's what Lego does with its sets: any set has a number, an exact parts list and its instructions, so you can rebuild it years later. datom does that for data.

The quote is often credited to Connie Morella (2006), but older versions exist; hence "as the saying goes".
:::
